findings.clean-os-g1-009: On the current Windows/no-fcntl path, event-log rollover lacks a shared cross-instance/process lock. A deterministic interleaving of two sinks can overwrite a retained canonical generation; POSIX flock closes this specific writer/writer race.
findings.clean-os-g1-010: Canonical readers such as iter_call_events and planner_verdict_was_persisted enumerate generation pathnames without events.lock. A valid concurrent rollover can move a retained generation outside the saved pathname set even on POSIX, yielding incomplete call history or a false persistence negative that can authorize a duplicate verdict re-emission attempt.
findings.clean-os-g1-007-migration: Blanket destructive schema<=6 Mission View rebuild is too broad. Public release history retained generations from day one, but legacy schema lineage completeness is unproved and current v4 migration deliberately preserves projected state without logs. Rebuild only with provable completeness; otherwise retain a legacy baseline and establish a future cursor/barrier.
findings.shared_fix_direction: Use one cross-platform event_log_locked/stable-generation snapshot primitive for append/rotation and correctness-sensitive readers/reconciliation, preserving events.lock -> mission-view.lock.

exact_next_action: Add literal concurrent-rotation regressions for iter_call_events and planner_verdict_was_persisted, combine them with a two-independent-sink fake-Windows rollover test, and specify one cross-platform event_log_locked/stable-generation snapshot API. Compare lock-through-scan versus handle-pinning after verifying Windows rename semantics; then revise schema-7 migration tests around the existing v4-preservation contract and retain the projection Variant A/B readback and candidate-008 durability branches.
